A faster and steadier `sst dev`, above all under load, your functions' output in their CloudWatch log groups if you ask for it, and an `sst deploy --policy` that stops before anything changes. Still built on upstream [v4.17.2](https://github.com/anomalyco/sst/releases/tag/v4.17.2).

Thanks to [@rogueturnip](https://github.com/rogueturnip), who load-tested `sst dev` with up to 100 requests at once through a Live authorizer ([#125](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/issues/125)), reported what broke, and sent eight of the pull requests below.

### New

- **`sst dev` can print what your functions and tasks print in their CloudWatch log groups.** Set `SST_DEV_CLOUDWATCH_LOGS=true`, and each line is printed in the invocation it belongs to, under its request ID, with `ERROR Invoke Error {...}` after a failure. So Logs Insights, metric filters and log subscriptions see your local output as they would when the function is deployed, and, as there, what a function prints after it returns shows in its next invocation. A `Workflow`'s log group now also gets its stub's own lines. ([#120](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/120))
- **`sst dev` sends the first copy of a function's reply over the WebSocket it already has open,** which gets it to the function in AWS about 50 ms sooner, and about 115 ms sooner for a 128 KB reply. Up to 15 a second go that way. If AppSync doesn't acknowledge one within half a second, throttles it, or the WebSocket has closed, it's sent over HTTPS too, and copies sent again always go over HTTPS. `SST_DEV_HTTP_PUBLISH=true` keeps everything on HTTPS. ([#153](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/153))
- **`sst dev` warns when your AWS account's Lambda concurrency is low.** When the region has fewer than 100 unreserved concurrent executions, it says so once after a deploy that runs a function Live, and how to raise the quota. The check reads `lambda:GetAccountSettings`; a deploy role without it gets no warning. ([#132](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/132), by [@rogueturnip](https://github.com/rogueturnip))

### Fixes

- **`sst dev` no longer drops, holds up or delays an invocation.** A worker that exits with invocations queued for it, or just as one is handed to it, is started again for them. A build holds up only the function being built. A worker gets its invocation without waiting for the ping, and a reply stops being resent once the next invocation arrives. ([#130](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/130), by [@rogueturnip](https://github.com/rogueturnip))
- **Saving a file in `sst dev` no longer fails the requests in flight.** A function that's rebuilt finishes the invocation its worker is running before the worker is replaced, instead of the worker being killed mid-request. Only the worker of the environment used last starts again straight away, and workers that exit, stop or reload are cleaned up. ([#157](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/157); [#135](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/issues/135), reported by [@rogueturnip](https://github.com/rogueturnip))
- **An invocation whose worker can't start fails straight away,** instead of at Lambda's timeout, with an init error that says whether the function's build failed or its runtime couldn't run it. ([#155](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/155), [#176](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/176); [#139](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/issues/139), reported by [@rogueturnip](https://github.com/rogueturnip))
- **An invocation that `sst dev` doesn't answer now fails.** An API Gateway or function URL request still gets a 500, which now says `sst dev` didn't answer. A direct invoke, or an event source such as a queue, gets an `SstDevUnavailable` error, so the event is retried, and can reach a dead-letter queue, instead of being dropped. ([#129](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/129), by [@rogueturnip](https://github.com/rogueturnip))
- **`sst dev` sends a message to a function in AWS again when AppSync throttled it or didn't answer.** A reply, ping or reboot that got a 429, a 5xx or a dropped connection is retried, and each try is signed and timed out, so a publish can't hang. ([#128](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/128), by [@rogueturnip](https://github.com/rogueturnip))
- **A Node.js function in `sst dev` no longer waits about 300 ms on each call to the runtime API** on Node.js 26.7.0, whose `fetch` held those calls on a kept-alive connection until a timer fired. The local worker uses `http.request` now. ([#137](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/137), by [@rogueturnip](https://github.com/rogueturnip); [#136](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/issues/136))
- **A long `sst dev` session no longer grows for as long as it runs:**
  - A Lambda environment is forgotten 15 minutes after its worker stops, and the UI forgets that worker's start time and color with it. A new worker no longer takes the color of one still running. ([#159](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/159), [#168](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/168))
  - Each terminal pane keeps its last 10,000 lines, and the client that talks to your functions in AWS remembers a bounded number of messages. ([#158](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/158))
  - `.sst/log/sst.log` moves to `sst.log.1` at 50 MB and starts again. A command no longer leaves its temporary log in your system's temp folder. ([#169](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/169))
  - Each function keeps its newest 100 invocation logs in `.sst/log/lambda/`, and a log file is closed with its invocation. ([#131](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/131), by [@rogueturnip](https://github.com/rogueturnip))
  - A message to a function in AWS no longer takes 128 KB up front for each packet. ([#138](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/138), by [@rogueturnip](https://github.com/rogueturnip))

  Reported in [#134](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/issues/134) by [@rogueturnip](https://github.com/rogueturnip).
- **`sst dev` rebuilds the functions a change affects together, and picks up changed build options.** The functions that use a changed file are built once, as a batch, and a change to a function's `nodejs` options, such as `esbuild`, `banner` or `format`, applies on the next rebuild instead of after a restart. ([#118](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/118))
- **`sst dev` no longer logs an error when a Lambda environment says it's there a second time,** which happens when its first invocation is handled before its init. ([#156](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/156))
- **`sst deploy --policy` previews before it updates, so a mandatory policy stops the deploy before anything is created or changed,** as the policy packs docs say. Before, what the policy didn't stop could deploy first. A deploy with `--policy` takes longer, as Pulumi runs your app twice, and an advisory warning is shown once. ([#167](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/167))
- **`sst dev --policy` shows a policy pack's advisory warnings,** as `sst deploy --policy` does. ([#166](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/166))
- **A `Mysql` without a `version` can be created again.** RDS no longer offers MySQL 8.0.40, the old default. The default is now `"8.0"`, and RDS picks its current 8.0 minor. A database that's already deployed doesn't change. ([#141](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/141))

### Changes

- **`sst upgrade` and `sst init` stay within the CLI's major version.** Once 5.0 is out, a 4.x CLI upgrades to the newest 4.x, and writes 4.x into a new project. `sst upgrade <version>` moves to another major. ([#142](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/142))
- **The CLI installs `.sst/platform` with Bun 1.4.2**, instead of 1.2.1. The first command after you update downloads it. ([#143](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/143))

### Also

- The `Function` docs explain turning `dev` off for an authorizer, which saves a round trip to your machine on each request ([#133](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/133), by [@rogueturnip](https://github.com/rogueturnip)).
- The docs site's changelog lists this fork's releases, and is updated with each one ([#175](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/175); [#170](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/issues/170), reported by [@AlperSakarya](https://github.com/AlperSakarya)).
- CI runs the components' tests ([#140](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/140), [#165](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/165)), and the automatic review uses a model that's still offered ([#160](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/160), [#161](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/161), [#162](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/162)).

### Install

```bash
npm install sst@npm:@sst-community/sst@4.22.0
```

To switch an existing project:

1. Check that `node --version` shows `v22` or later, wherever you run `sst`, CI included.
2. Set its dependency to `"sst": "npm:@sst-community/sst@4.22.0"` and reinstall.

For a project that isn't JavaScript, install the CLI globally. It still needs Node.js 22 or later, to run `sst.config.ts`:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sst-community/sst/main/install | bash
```
